title: Script action bodies write into a disabled package's objects: ctx.api insert succeeds where REST refuses 404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED
body:
repo:hotcrm#1 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAnPkgK6CWrJa6t7Fk5

Found by the hotcrm lane's probe for hotcrm#2618 (report: hotcrm#2618 comment 6952320824) on @objectstack 18.5.0, local SQLite. Read in code on objectstack `main` fc5913e117.

## What happens

Package A (Project Delivery) depends on package B (Order to Cash). B is disabled with `PATCH /api/v1/packages/<B>/disable` (200). Then:

- `POST /api/v1/data/crm_billing_milestone` (B's object) → 404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, as designed.
- `POST /api/v1/actions/crm_project/prepare_billing` (A's script action, A enabled) → 200. Its body's `ctx.api.object('crm_billing_milestone').insert(...)` **wrote a row into B's disabled object**, and B's own beforeInsert hook (`billing_milestone_row_stamp`) ran on it. The row was there after B was re-enabled.

## Why, in code

The disabled-package refusal lives at the doors, not in the engine. `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` ~546–565 (`refuseUnexposedDataAction`) says it outright: "the engine serves a disabled package's objects". `isObjectPackageDisabled` is called only from REST meta routes, `protocol-authoring-refusals.ts` and `effective-object-permissions.ts`. A sandboxed script's `ctx.api` (`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts`) reaches the engine without passing that gate.

Related: #25296 (closed: the action door ran a disabled package's own action) and #33527 (open: whether withdrawn packages stay armed). This one is a third door: an enabled package's body writing into a disabled package.

## Asked

A disabled package's objects refuse writes (and reads) from every non-system caller, script bodies included, with the same `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`. Decide whether `isSystem` writes are exempt, and say so in the ledger.

## Done when

The probe above answers the action with a refusal naming the disabled object, and nothing lands in it.
